newsitem.title: USA: Stocks mostly lower but technology shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Stocks mostly lower but technology shares rise.

text.p: Stocks were mostly lower in quiet pre-Thanksgiving trading Wednesday, although a revitalised technology sector lent stability to the market.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 33.17 points at 6,495.24. In the broader market, declining issues led advances by small margin on light volume of 227 million shares.
The technology-laced Nasdaq composite index was up 2.01 at 1,283.21, while the Anerican Stock Exchange index lost 0.58 at 587.75.
"The techs are resuming leadership after a couple days break. But the Dow itself is taking a well-needed pause," said James Cramer, president of Cramer Co.
"I do give thanks to the Dow for not going up and up and up," he said. "Every time it cools off, the rally becomes more sustainable."
Among technology shares, International Business Machines was up 1-1/4 at 159-1/4, Intel rose 2-1/4 to 126, Cisco was up 1/8 to 67-3/8 and Microsoft rose 1-1/4 to 155.
Analysts said the bulk of the activity likely took place in the first hour of trading after a battery of economic reports.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was steady at Tuesday's close of 6.45 percent after falling slightly initially on news that third-quarter Gross Domestic Product growth was revised downward to 2.0 percent from 2.2 percent.
Also reported was weekly jobless claims, which were unchanged at 342,000, and higher than the forecast 336,000 for the Nov. 23 week.
"There's not much to crow about. The market is giving back some of its gains," said Alan Ackerman of Fahnestock & Co.
Financial markets will be closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. Stock markets will hold an abbreviated session Friday, with trading ending at 1 p.m. EST/1800 GMT.
Oil company stocks were generally lower on profit-taking after recent gains. Texaco lost 2 to 98-7/8, Exxon was off 1-3/8 to 93-1/2, Chevron fell 1-1/4 to 66-7/8 and Mobil slipped 1/2 to 120-7/8.

Crude oil was up 18 cents at $23.80 a barrel in early afternoon on the New York Mercantile Exchange amid indications that the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, which is meeting in Vienna, appeared set to hold the line on oil exports for the next six months. The meeting is expected to end on Thursday.
Among individual issues, America Online added 2-3/4 to 35-3/8 after Cowen & Co. upgraded the company's stock.
Walt Disney lost 2-1/4 to 74, giving back Tuesday's rally following an upbeat earnings report.
Forrester Research, which provides products and services that gauge how technology affects business, surged 5-3/4 to 21-3/4 in its first day of trading.
